'''Norman Grant Gaylord''' (born '''Norman Gershon Goldstein'''; February 16, 1923 – September 18, 2007) was an American industrial [[chemist]] and research scientist. He was credited with playing a key role in the development of the gas-permeable rigid [[contact lens]] which allows [[oxygen]] to reach the wearer's cornea.<ref name=bc>{{cite web |url=https://archive.boston.com/news/globe/obituaries/articles/2007/09/23/norman_gaylord_84_helped_develop_type_of_contact_lens/|title=Norman Gaylord, 84; helped develop type of contact lens|access-date=2007-10-06 |author=Pearce, Jeremy|date=2007-09-23 |work=(New York Times News Service) |publisher=[[The Boston Globe]]}}</ref>

A native of [[Brooklyn]], he was a graduate of [[City College of New York|City College]] and received his [[Sc.D.|doctorate]] in [[polymer chemistry]] from the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]], now NYU Tandon School of Engineering. He legally changed his name in the 1940s.<ref>''U.S. Social Security Applications and Claims Index, 1936-2007''; Social Security Administration.</ref>  For his contribution to the production of lenses Gaylord received in 1985 Founder's Award from the [[American Academy of Optometry]].<ref name="NYT"/>

Gaylord died in the [[Florida]] city of [[Boynton Beach, Florida|Boynton Beach]] at the age of 84.<ref name="NYT">{{cite news|last1=Pearce|first1=Jeremy|title=Norman Gaylord, a Chemist, Is Dead at 84|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/09/21/us/21gaylord.html|accessdate=June 19, 2017|work=The New York Times|date=September 21, 2007}}</ref><ref name="ACS">{{Cite web |url=http://www.polyacs.org/143.html |title=American Chemical Society; Division of Polymer Chemistry; Dr. Norman G. Gaylord, d.-2007 |access-date=2017-06-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160418045823/http://www.polyacs.org/143.html |archive-date=2016-04-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
